task_description: You write the git commit message for a diff. Answer with one line in Conventional Commits format: type(scope): summary. type is one of feat, fix, chore, refactor, test, perf, docs, build, ci, style. scope is the module, folder or component the diff touches. The summary is imperative, lower case, under 72 characters, and says what changed and why when the diff shows it. Add ! after the scope for a breaking change. Output only the commit message line. Types: feat = new behaviour for users; fix = corrects wrong behaviour; refactor = same behaviour, restructured code; perf = same output, faster; chore = dependencies, tooling, lint or build config; test = tests only; docs = documentation only. Adding validation, checks or guards that stop wrong input or wrong behaviour is fix. Changes to configuration, build, bundler, CI or infrastructure settings are chore, even when they enable something new. The scope is the main module, class or folder the diff touches.
llm_as_a_judge_instructions: Output 'good' if the predicted commit message (1) follows type(scope): summary on one line, (2) has the same type as the reference or an equally correct one, and (3) describes the main change in the diff accurately without inventing changes. It does not need to match the reference wording. Otherwise output 'bad'.
synthetic_data_generation_instructions: Each input has two parts. First one line: `Repository: <short description of the codebase> (<language in lower case>)`, for example `Repository: Flask REST API (python)` or `Repository: Rust CLI tool - file processing (rust)`. Then a blank line and a realistic unified git diff: `diff --git a/<path> b/<path>`, `---`/`+++` lines and `@@` hunk headers, 5-60 changed lines in one to three files, from a real-world codebase (web APIs, CLIs, data pipelines, frontends, libraries, infra scripts, build and CI config). The Repository line describes the codebase only. It never names the kind of change or the conclusion (no 'bug fix', 'performance', 'refactor', 'breaking change'), and code comments in the diff do not announce it either: the type must be worked out from the code. Vary the change kind, the file paths, the size and the structure (modified lines, new files, deleted code, renamed functions). The answer is exactly one Conventional Commits line, type(scope): summary, with nothing else. Choose the type from what the diff does: feat = a new capability or option; fix = the old code visibly produced a wrong result, a crash, a leak or a security hole and the diff corrects it; the summary never claims a bug that the old code does not show; refactor = the code is restructured and observable behaviour stays exactly the same (renames, extracted helpers, merged checks, dispatch tables, newer API with the same result); never label such a diff fix or perf; perf = same behaviour but faster or using less memory; chore = dependency bumps, tooling, lint or build config, housekeeping; test = only test files change; docs = only documentation or docstrings change. The scope is the module, folder or component the diff touches (omit it only when the change is repository-wide, such as a top-level README). The summary is imperative, lower case, under 72 characters, and says what changed and, when the diff shows it, why. Put ! after the scope only when the diff breaks a public interface of library or service code (a changed signature or return type, a removed option). test, docs and chore commits never take !: if the change kind asks for a breaking change but the type is test, docs or chore, write an ordinary non-breaking change of that type.
